discrepancies.claim: Across the 53,737 3-class folds, 25,426 (47.3%) contain a single class
discrepancies.filter_source: every run_id in prediction_folds_long.csv (3,738 run_ids, 50 method names, all 18 Shambhala P/Q variants)
discrepancies.filter_recomputed: run_id restricted to the 2,234-approach analysis set
discrepancies.cause: the published figure counted folds for approaches the article never analyses; 20,343 of the 53,737 belong to the 17 non-canonical Shambhala P/Q variants, and the residual 648 to 34_arsyn and 38_harman, which fail pct_samples_allNA < 5 (20,343 + 648 = 20,991 = 53,737 - 32,746). The canonical shambhala_P0std_Q0std is kept, as 20_shambhala, and contributes 1,200 of the 32,746
discrepancies.direction: the conclusion is unchanged -- single-class folds are still about half the population -- only the counts move

discrepancies.claim: single-class folds have median macro F1 0.952; two-class 0.648; three-class 0.830
discrepancies.direction: the ordering is unchanged: two-class folds remain the hardest and single-class folds the easiest

discrepancies.claim: Spearman between the full metric and the multiclass-only mean is 0.812 over the 1,981 approaches with at least three multiclass folds
discrepancies.recomputed: 0.815 over 2,058 such approaches; 0.810 over all 2,174 carrying both
discrepancies.filter_source: fold aggregates computed over the unrestricted fold table
discrepancies.filter_recomputed: fold aggregates over the analysis set only
discrepancies.cause: same population difference; the approach count rises because restricting the fold table does not remove approaches, only foreign run_ids
discrepancies.direction: unchanged conclusion: the two cuts agree closely and neither reverses the other

discrepancies.claim: Per-batch detail for S0_no_removal/softimpute/29_combat_ref/post0: 10 of the 24 folds are single-class; the hard folds are GPL96_FFPE_Unknown and RNASeq_FF_PolyA
discrepancies.recomputed: 13 of 24 folds are single-class; the three hardest multiclass folds are GPL96_FFPE_Unknown (F1 0.462), RNASeq_FFPE_PolyA (0.698) and RNASeq_FF_PolyA (0.718)
discrepancies.cause: the two quoted folds and their values reproduce exactly; the single-class count and the identity of the second-hardest fold do not

discrepancies.claim: multiclass-only F1 across harshness tiers: H = 11.2, p = 0.0037
discrepancies.filter_source: f1_mc_mean computed over the unrestricted fold table
discrepancies.cause: same population difference; every other row of the tier table reproduces exactly, including the 2-class AUC result (H = 1.5, p = 0.48, not significant)

discrepancies.claim: Top by raw-subtracted margin: K_ffpe_only / knn / 06_combat_seq / post0
discrepancies.recomputed: 06_combat_seq and 08_inmoose_combatseq are an exact tie at that (strat, imp, post_rm): margin 0.439161, gain +0.457154 for both
discrepancies.cause: two implementations of the same algorithm return identical Group M values; the sort order between them is arbitrary
discrepancies.direction: quote both, or say that the two implementations agree exactly -- which is itself a positive control worth a sentence

discrepancies.claim: Cells not traceable to the generator: 8 in the main notebook, 43 in the narrow-set notebook, 29 in the deep-analysis notebook
discrepancies.recomputed: 12 / 50 / 53 hand-written, plus 6 / 12 / 52 generator cells edited in place
discrepancies.filter_recomputed: tools/extract_hand_written_cells.py, generator run at the same --date-tag, normalized comparison, NEAR threshold 0.90
discrepancies.cause: the earlier count did not separate edited generator cells from untouched ones; an edited cell still looks like the generator's, so regeneration reverts it without saying so
discrepancies.direction: materially larger: 185 cells must survive regeneration, not 80
